note:
# Census pass: P-E-2019-1902917-3fb00373

## What the paper is
A replacement-cost valuation of the Tennessee Valley Authority power system. The short-run
model splits cost and benefit into economic and environmental halves (Figures 1 and 2), the
long-run model adds a five-criterion AHP ranking (Figure 3, Tables 2 and 3), a case study
applies both to the TVA, and one sensitivity sweep closes the argument (Figure 4). Twenty-four
pages, ten printed exhibits, and an appendix holding a borrowed map and two pasted grids from
a Chinese publication.

## Coverage arithmetic
Sixteen measured regions on eleven of the twenty-four pages: ten exhibits (five figures, five
tables), six excluded, zero unaccounted. The exclusions are the two tails of split grids (the
last two rows of Table 2 at the top of p12, the last three rows of the appendix cost table at
the top of p23), one table fragment below the scanned revenue grid, the reference-list lines
the pass boxes on p21, and the two running-head bands that survive as vector regions on pages
23 and 24.

## The finding: the appendix is pasted, and it says so
Three appendix exhibits, three provenances, none of them authored here. The map is a
Google-Maps-style render of the TVA service area with its key compressed into a single typeset
line under the picture. The cost table is a typeset Chinese grid numbered in its source's own
scheme - "Tab. 3-2" with a footnote marker - and it is the only exhibit in the paper with a
merged header cell. The revenue table is a SCAN OF A BOOK PAGE: it carries the source chapter
head "第 4 章 TVA 电力的开发成就与问题" above the grid and a diagonal split corner cell, and
the scan is cut in two, with years 1957-1947 printed above years 1966-1958, so the page reads
backwards halfway down.

That gives this paper the lane's first foreign-running-head exhibit, and its first
diagonal-header table.

## Geometry: one recipe, three schematics
Figures 1, 2 and 3 are the same drawing: a rooted box tree, branches as right-angle rules, all
labels live text, and a grey fill applied to some leaves and not others with no key - Figure 1
fills four boxes, Figure 2 three, and the paper never explains it. Figure 3 is the only place
the model fans out: five environmental children that are exactly the five criteria Tables 2
and 3 then weigh. Figure 4 is a stock MATLAB export - in-plot title "sensitivity", both axes
titled, light grid, two fitted lines labelled in place by gtext - and it is the only exhibit in
the paper with printed tick numbers. Nothing is multipanel, nothing is three-dimensional,
nothing has a colourbar, and the only legend in the paper is the map's swatch line.

## Captions: two dialects, no verbs, and a whole caption missing
Figures caption with a fullwidth colon ("Figure 1："), tables with an ASCII colon and no space
before the number ("Table2:"). All ten are noun phrases of three to fourteen words: no finite
verb, no unit, no condition, no conclusion. The units that matter are inside the grids - Table
1 has a Unit column, Table 3 writes "$4,120million" in a cell, the appendix table puts 10k kW
and USD/kW in its header strings.

The break worth recording: the appendix exhibits are captioned on the page and the text layer
returns none of it. The layer holds only "Appendices", the two deixis lines and the Matlab
listing; the map's title line and the "Tab. 3-2" caption exist as pixels. #172 broke by
substitution (Shanghai printed, "Shanghui" in the layer); this paper breaks by omission of an
entire caption.

## Counting and citation
Named by number: the four body figures, plus Table 2 - the only grid the prose ever points at,
and the only exhibit pointed at twice. Named by deixis alone: the appendix map and the appendix
cost table. Never named in any form: Table 1, Table 3 and the scanned revenue table. Pointers
are period-spelled ("Figure.1") and always end the
sentence on the number, same page as the art. The appendix abandons numbering altogether: three
bare lead-ins - "This is the map of the power station:", "These are the cost tables:", "These
are Matlab codes:" - and the third one introduces code that is not an exhibit while the two
scanned tables that follow it get no sentence at all.

## What the grids are like
Table 1 is the paper's notation list, booktabs, split across a page break with its caption and
header at the foot of p4. Table 2 is the AHP ranking standards, seven columns, five rank rows,
each score in brackets under the rank, and it loses its last two rows to a bare boxed strip at
the top of p12 with no repeated header. Table 3 is the only grid with a vertical rule and no
outer box. Nothing decimal-aligns; Table 2 stores ranges with a fullwidth tilde. The layer
scrambles Table 2's cell order and truncates the Matlab listing, so quotes from that grid have
to be taken row by row.

## Sizes
Sizes run from 0.093 (the nine-row result grid on p16) to 0.304 (Table 1's fifteen-row
notation body). The three schematics that carry the model sit in the narrow band
0.138-0.155, the borrowed appendix material above them at 0.188-0.245, and the largest
region in the paper is a notation list - so size tracks neither the model nor the
argument, it tracks how much paper the content happened to need.

## The layer's own defects
Table captions absent from the layer (see above); Table 2's cells out of order; the code cut
mid-line at the page break; the running head is live text with the folio inside it ("Team
#1902917  Page 23 of 24"), which is why the pass boxes a thin vector band on pages 23 and 24.
rules: Sixteen measured regions on eleven of the twenty-four pages, and they close exactly: ten printed exhibits (five figures, five tables), six excluded regions and no unaccounted box - the paper is long enough that the appendix, the reference list and the folio rules all leave residue for the pass to hand back [place.section_path].

The appendix is the first in the lane to print ANOTHER DOCUMENT'S PAGE: the third appendix exhibit is a scan that carries the source book's chapter running head above the table, so one of this paper's exhibits literally contains a foreign header [place.section_path].
Family mix of the five figures: flowchart-or-schematic 3 (Figures 1, 2, 3), line 1 (Figure 4, the sensitivity sweep) and map-or-plan-view 1 (the borrowed appendix map) [geometry.family].

The three schematics are ONE DRAWING RECIPE APPLIED THREE TIMES: a rooted box tree whose branches are plain right-angle rules, every box live text, and light grey fill applied to some leaves and not others with no key - Figure 1 fills four boxes, Figure 2 fills three, and neither paper explains the shading [geometry.family].

The trees carry the paper's whole model: Figure 1 breaks short-run cost into economic and environmental halves three tiers deep, Figure 2 mirrors it for benefit with one tier fewer, and Figure 3's environmental branch has FIVE children that are exactly the five criteria the AHP grids of Tables 2 and 3 then weigh [geometry.family].
Nothing in the paper is multipanel: all five figures are single-panel, none shares an axis, and there is no composite exhibit anywhere in twenty-four pages [geometry.panel_count].

Only one exhibit has a legend and it is not a legend box: the appendix map carries a single typeset key line UNDER the picture - the title 'May 2005 map of TVA sites' followed by three colour swatches for dam, nuclear and fossil - while all four body figures are labelled in place with no key at all [geometry.legend].
No colourbar anywhere in the paper, in a census whose two neighbouring passes both recorded one [geometry.colorbar].
Nothing is drawn in three dimensions - no perspective bars, no surface mesh, no isometric frame - so the three_d field of this census is empty by fact [geometry.three_d].

Printed numbers appear in ONE figure only: Figure 4's MATLAB export, which carries a full tick set on both axes (y 3 to 6 by 0.5, x 0 to 1 by 0.1). The three schematics print none, and the appendix map's numerals are interstate shields rather than coordinates [geometry.printed_numbers].

All five figures draw their labels inside the art and the labelling is load-bearing: the box labels of Figures 1 to 3 carry the model's variable names (C, C1, C2, C12, C121...), Figure 4 labels its two fitted lines in place, and the map's place names and state initials are rasterised into the borrowed picture [geometry.data_labels].

Caption side splits by exhibit type and the split is absolute: all four body figures print their caption BELOW the art, all five tables print theirs ABOVE, and the three appendix exhibits carry no text-layer caption at all [caption.position].

Two numbering dialects in one paper: the figures use a FULLWIDTH colon ('Figure 1：') while the tables use an ASCII colon and drop the space before the number ('Table2: Ranking standards...', 'Table3: The ranks...'), so no two table captions are punctuated alike [caption.numbering].

Captions are short and verbless: three to fourteen words, every one a noun phrase with no finite verb, no condition and no conclusion, so voice is unassignable across all ten exhibits [caption.voice].

No caption names a variable, an axis or a parameter value: the AHP captions speak of 'values' changes of different indexes' and leave the five criteria to the header block, so the caption field's variable_count is zero throughout [caption.variables].

No caption gives a unit either; the units live in the grids instead - Table 1's 'Unit' column ('$', 'm2', 'm3'), Table 3's in-cell '$4,120million', and the appendix cost table's header strings (10k kW, USD/kW) [caption.units].

A NEW BREAK MODE: the appendix's three exhibits are captioned ON THE PAGE but the text layer returns none of those captions - the layer holds only the two deixis lines and the code, so the map title and the 'Tab. 3-2' caption exist as pixels alone. #172's break was a substitution; this one is an omission of a whole caption [caption.verbatim].

Citation splits three ways. Named by NUMBER: the four body figures and Table 2, which is the only grid the prose ever points at, and the only exhibit pointed at twice. Named by DEIXIS with no number at all: the appendix map and the appendix cost table ('This is the map of the power station:', 'These are the cost tables:'). Never named in any form: Table 1, Table 3 and the scanned revenue table [mention.count].

Pointer spelling is the period kind: 'Figure.1', 'Figure.2', 'Figure.3', 'Figure.4' - with a period and no space - and the two stray table pointers print 'Table2' once and 'Table.2' once, so the same exhibit is spelled two ways on two pages [mention.style].

Every pointer is same-page and sentence-initial: no exhibit is announced before the page it sits on, none is named after it, and the lead sentence always ends on the number ('...we use diagram in Figure.1', '...can be viewed in Figure.2.') [mention.lead_pages].

Only Figure 4 is read after the fact, and the reading is a value rather than a trend: 'both of them converge to 5 with the growth of a' names the ordinate off the plot; the three schematics and the map get no reading sentence at all [mention.trail_sentence].

The appendix uses the lane's first all-deixis citation scheme: three bare lead-ins with no number in any of them - 'This is the map of the power station:', 'These are the cost tables:', 'These are Matlab codes:' - and the third points at code that is not an exhibit, leaving the two scanned tables after it entirely unannounced [mention.lead_pattern].

Table rules are not house style: Table 1 and Table 2 are booktabs (heavy top, heavy header rule, heavy bottom, no verticals), Table 3 has ONE VERTICAL rule and no outer box, and both appendix tables are fully boxed grids with every vertical drawn [table.rule_style].

Merged cells appear exactly once - the appendix cost table's cost column split into 'then-current US dollars' and 'constant 1982 prices' under one spanned header - and the paper's only diagonal split corner cell sits on the scanned revenue table, whose corner prints '项目' above the diagonal and '年份' below [table.merged_cells].

Two of the five tables break and NEITHER repeats its header: Table 1's caption and header print at the foot of one page and its fifteen symbol rows at the top of the next, and Table 2 loses its last two rank rows to the top of the following page as a separate boxed strip with no header at all [table.continued].

No grid in the paper decimal-aligns anything: Table 2 stores its cells as ranges with a fullwidth tilde ('0.3～0.5', 'under0.1') so nothing lines up, and the appendix tables throw thousands separators and dashes for missing data into the same numeric columns [table.decimal_aligned].

Exhibits are allocated by argument stage, one type per section, and the pattern is stable: the symbols section takes the notation table, the model sections take the three schematics, the evaluation section takes the ranking grid, the solution section takes the result grid, sensitivity takes the only plotted chart, and the appendix takes the borrowed map plus the two pasted grids [place.section_kind].
Nine of the ten exhibits own their page; the one shared page is p22, where the map and the cost table are stacked under two separate lead-ins. None is landscape [place.page_order].

Sizes run 0.093 (Table 3) to 0.304 (Table 1's fifteen-row body), and the ranking is not by importance: the three schematics that carry the model sit at 0.138-0.155, the borrowed appendix material at 0.188-0.245, and the largest region in the paper is a notation list [place.area_frac].

The layer mangles the one table that matters: Table 2's cell order is scrambled (the range cells of different rows interleave, '0.7AC～' and '（3）' arrive out of column), and the Matlab listing is cut off mid-line at the page break - transcribed quotes for that grid therefore have to be taken row by row rather than read off the layer in order [table.rows].

Booktabs throughout - heavy top rule, heavy rule under the header, heavy bottom rule, no verticals, no zebra, no merged cells - and the unit column carries every unit ('$', 'm2', 'm3', '$/m2') so no unit appears in the caption. Five columns - name, year built, capacity in 10k kW, and a COST COLUMN SPLIT INTO TWO SPANNED SUBCOLUMNS ('at then-current US dollars' / 'at constant 1982 prices'), which is the paper's only merged header cell - over eight plant rows (Watts Bar 1942 through Gallatin 1956), full grid with vertical and horizontal rules, no zebra, no totals, decimals not aligned. Six columns (the year plus five money columns - power revenue, total revenue, rent and other revenue, net power revenue, operating expense) over eleven year rows 1957 down to 1947, full outer box with every vertical rule drawn, and the paper's ONLY DIAGONAL SPLIT CORNER CELL, carrying '项目' above the diagonal and '年份' below it.
